Tell me how you make that please.

Sure! There's a few different ingredients you can sub or leave out depending on your tastes.

This makes about 3 servings.

Ingredients

  • 1/2lb boneless skinless chicken breast, cubed as big or small as you want on your spoon
  • 2-3 teaspoons olive oil
  • 1/2 medium onion, diced
  • 1/2 (red) bell pepper, diced (anaheim or poblano is fine too)
  • 1 jalapeño, diced (and seeded if you're a wimp like me)
  • 2-3 garlic cloves, finely chopped
  • 1 TB Cornmeal (for thickening)
  • 1 can black beans, drained and rinsed
  • 1 can red enchilada sauce
  • 1/2 can petite diced tomatoes (reg. diced is fine, I just like smaller pieces)
  • 1/2 cup frozen corn (drained canned corn would work too)
  • 1 1/2 - 2 cups chicken stock or water + bullion
  • 1/2 teaspoon Cumin
  • 1/8th teaspoon ground chipotle powder (optional but delicious)
  • Ground red pepper if you don't like to feel your lips
  • Salt & Pepper to taste

Optional Toppings

  • Fresh chopped cilantro (coriander depending where you live)
  • Chopped green onion
  • Cheese would be wonderful with this, but cheese hates me
  • Tortilla/taco chip crumbs
  • Maybe sour cream? Again with the dairy...

Directions

Heat oil in a large skillet or dutch oven over med-high heat. Add the chicken and let it brown for a couple of minutes before stirring. Brown on another side. It's okay if it doesn't cook all the way through.

Add the onion and peppers and cook for about 5 mins to soften. Add the garlic and quickly sprinkle in the cornmeal. Stir this constantly for about 20-30 seconds until you can smell the garlic. Don't let the garlic or cornmeal burn!

Pour in about half of the broth, it should immediately begin to boil. Scrape the bottom of the pan with a spatula to deglaze those delicious bits of browned stuff.

Add the rest of the broth, tomatoes, enchilada sauce, beans and spices. Bring to simmer and cook for 15 mins to let the flavors meld. Add the corn and let it heat through.

I like to use corn because the sweetness helps balance the salty spicy richness of the rest of the soup. It also adds nice color. If you don't want to use corn, consider adding a teaspoon or two of sugar.

Cilantro, green onions and taco chip crumbs are my favorite toppings
